title: Hubble Finds the Most Distant Star Ever Seen
description: With this observation, the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope has established an extraordinary new benchmark: detecting the light of a star that existed within the first billion years after the Universe’s birth in the Big Bang (at a redshift of 6.2) — the most distant individual star ever seen. This sets up a major target for the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope in its first year.
credit: NASA, ESA, B. Welch (JHU), D. Coe (STScI), A. Pagan (STScI)
name: Distant Star
